body.statement: There are constants \(0<c_{\beta,D}\le C_{\beta,D}<\infty\) such that for all admissible \(n,m,\tau\), \[c_{\beta,D}\ell\min\{1,(m/n)^{\varkappa}\}\le\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\le C_{\beta,D}\ell\min\{1,[m\log(2m)/n]^{\varkappa}\}.\] The explicit total learner \(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{tail}}\) attains the upper bound, including its all-control branch for sparse or empty cell-arm samples, and the lower bound ranges over the same \(\mathcal H_{\beta,D}(m)\) against every learner in \(\mathfrak A_{n,m}\). Equivalently, its upper rate is \(C_{\beta,D}\mathcal B_{\mathrm{CK}}(n,m,\tau)\). Moreover, along any admissible sequence with \(m/n\to0\) and \(\ell(m/n)^{\varkappa}\to0\), \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)/\mathcal B_{\mathrm{AW}}(n,m)\to\infty\); the regular additive-policy complexity scale does not represent extreme-tail regret even where the latter vanishes.
body.justification: The sandwich certifies a nontrivial full-class rate spine while exposing the exact logarithmic gap the headline question must close.
body.gap: The probability display in Theorem 3 of CarpentierKim2015 gives its adaptive single-tail upper rate, while Theorem 4 gives the adaptive lower bound and unavoidable log-log factor; neither result treats capacity-selected mixtures. The theorem identifies the coordinatewise known-envelope consequence after the separate absolute-exponent translation and proves that the regular mean-policy rate of AtheyWager2021 is asymptotically nonrepresentative for the moving extreme-quantile loss.
body.consumer: It gives safety-critical policy users a conservative sample-size rule even before the exact selection factor is resolved.
